rules: Use fundamental LEVELS as the fundamental leg, not deltas: 63-day TS_DELTA legs on $accrual_gap, $roa-$accrual_gap and $leverage went 0-for-3 on the cheap screen (|t| 0.41, 0.48, 0.90), while $roe/$roa/$accrual_gap levels carried the 5.117, 4.905 and 4.100 accepts.

Pair a fundamental rank with ONE raw statistic, not a nested correlation: CS_RANK($roe) minus a bare $volume rank scored 5.117 and minus a 10-day range TS_RANK 4.905, while fundamental x TS_CORR accepts scored only 0.082-0.641.

Keep price/volume windows in the 5-42 day band: the 63-day range-vs-volume corr screened at |t| 0.77 and scored 0.082 inside a spread, and a 126-day range/price-mean leg missed coverage at 0.874. Windows of 5/21 vs 63 as a RATIO (short over long, same field) is the exception that scored 4.100.
Range-vs-volume TS_CORR only lives with a transformed volume leg at 21 days: TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 21) vs $high-$low scored 2.993, while the plain $volume level version at 63 days screened dead.

Re-expressing the same quantity is never decorrelation: CS_RANK -> CS_ZSCORE on an identical inner tree hit rho 0.920, MAX(x,0) -> MIN(x,0) on the same leverage delta 0.842, and TS_MAX/TS_SUM of $volume(21) vs TS_STD/TS_MEAN of $volume(21) 0.914. Change a field or a window instead.

A fundamental rank-spread prefix sets rho by itself: two totally different price multipliers on a fundamental-minus-fundamental spread still hit rho 0.827, and RANK($roa) minus any 21-day price-position rank hit 0.814 and 0.815. That chassis is closed regardless of the price leg.
The 'where does close/open sit inside its N-day high-low range' family is exhausted at every window: one duplicate this round plus rho 0.965 from the sign-flipped distance-from-21-day-high version.

($high - $low) divided by a guarded single price ($high, $open, $low, or a TS_MEAN of one) drew three archive_subtree rejects at 5-7 shared nodes; normalising range by another range window or by the TS_MAX-TS_MIN span passed at 4.100 and 2.098.
